articles.title: Escalation In Middle East As Iran Hits Kurdish Bases In Erbil; Blast Hits Iraqi Militia HQ
articles.description: Iran has reportedly launched another drone strike against an Iranian Kurdish opposition group based in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region. Drones targeted a Komala Party base in Balisan, Erbil province, damaging buildings but causing no reported casualties. The attack follows a separate drone strike on a camp belonging to the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDPI) in Koya district. Since the US-Israeli war against Iran began on February 28, more than 1,000 drones and missiles have reportedly targeted the Kurdistan Region, launched by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Iran-backed Iraqi militias. Meanwhile, clashes between Iranian forces and Kurdish fighters have intensified in western Iran, adding to regional tensions as Tehran faces mounting military and security pressures.

articles.title: World News: Indian Diaspora in London Backs PM Modi Outside Indian High Commission
articles.description: Amid heightened political tensions in Delhi, members of the Indian diaspora gathered outside the Indian High Commission in London to express their support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The gathering featured slogans in support of Modi, India, and national pride, including chants of “Jai Shri Ram” and “Bharat Mata Ki Jai.” According to the report, the demonstration took place in response to protests organized by the BJP and Congress in Delhi. Participants at the London gathering voiced their concerns over what they described as attempts to damage India's reputation internationally through political criticism. The demonstrators argued that India is a democracy where citizens have access to legal remedies, including approaching courts and the Supreme Court, if they have grievances. They questioned why political disputes should be taken overseas and expressed the view that allegations should be supported by evidence. The gathering brought together members of the Indian community who wanted to publicly demonstrate their support for the prime minister and the country's development. Slogans such as “Modi Modi” and “Jai Bharat Mata Ki” echoed during the event, reflecting the participants' patriotic sentiments and political views. The development highlights how political debates within India can extend beyond national borders, prompting members of the Indian diaspora to organize demonstrations and express their opinions in international cities. London, home to a large Indian-origin community, has frequently served as a venue for public gatherings related to Indian political and social issues. The event also underscores the contrasting narratives surrounding political protests, national image, and democratic expression. The demonstrators' statements represent the views expressed by participants at the gathering.

articles.title: Delhi News: CJP Founder Abhijeet Deepke Arrested, Neha Bora Released by Delhi Police
articles.description: In a major development, Delhi Police has arrested CJP founder Abhijeet Deepke in connection with allegations of disturbing public peace ahead of a planned Tiranga March. According to the information provided in the report, action has been initiated against Deepke under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Abhijeet Deepke is scheduled to appear before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Court in New Delhi today. The court will consider the matter and determine the next legal steps. Further details regarding his custody or possible release will depend on the proceedings and the applicable legal process. The report states that Delhi Police had visited Deepke's residence before the proposed Tiranga March and informed him that permission for the march had not been granted. He was subsequently detained after the march began, and his arrest was reported later. Meanwhile, AISA president Neha Bora has been released by Delhi Police after the completion of formalities. According to the report, she had remained in police custody for approximately 13 hours. Both Neha Bora and Abhijeet Deepke had reportedly been detained under preventive provisions. The report also mentions that Ashutosh Ranga and Saurabh Das are in judicial custody in connection with separate developments involving the Tiranga and a flag-hoisting event at Jantar Mantar. The situation has drawn attention to police restrictions on public gatherings, the organization of marches, and the legal procedures surrounding preventive action. The outcome of Deepke's court appearance and any further official statements are expected to provide greater clarity on the case.
